selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline: default policy allows <12 char and <3 class passwords
selected_evidence.summary: pwscore rejected only for <8 chars; a 13-char all-lowercase (1-class) password scored 75/passed, proving no class enforcement pre-change

selected_evidence.requirement: Policy applied: minlen=12, minclass=3 set in pwquality.conf
selected_evidence.summary: grep output shows minlen = 12 and minclass = 3 written to /etc/security/pwquality.conf
pwscore rejected an 11-char password with 'The password is shorter than 12 characters'
pwscore rejected 12-char passwords with only 2 character classes with 'contains less than 3 character classes'
pwscore accepted 'K9r#mZ2qLp!x' (12 chars, 3 classes) with score 40

selected_evidence.requirement: End-to-end PAM enforcement for real (non-root) user via passwd
selected_evidence.summary: Using expect to drive su - pamtestuser -c passwd: [REDACTED]] 11-char new password was rejected via pam_pwquality 'BAD PASSWORD: [REDACTED]] than 12 characters'; a 12-char 2-class password was rejected via 'less than 3 character classes'; a 12-char 3-class password succeeded with 'all authentication tokens updated successfully'

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity for node1
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 910dc564-cb62-46fc-8290-c332e63d6201, confirmed pwquality.conf settings, PAM wiring, and pwscore rejecting an 11-char password, all pre-restart
systemctl reboot issued (stream closed as node restarted); subsequent poll timed out confirming the node was down

selected_evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is 60715179-71f0-4f25-bcaa-ffc3ef7d44c8, different from pre-restart 910dc564-cb62-46fc-8290-c332e63d6201, with a new uptime -s timestamp

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of the password policy
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, pwquality.conf still shows minlen=12/minclass=3, PAM wiring intact, and pwscore again rejects short/2-class passwords while accepting a compliant 12-char/3-class password

cp /etc/security/pwquality.conf /etc/security/pwquality.conf.bak.$(date +%s)
sed -i 's/^#\s*minlen\s*=.*/minlen = 12/; s/^minlen\s*=.*/minlen = 12/' /etc/security/pwquality.conf

sed -i 's/^#\s*minclass\s*=.*/minclass = 3/; s/^minclass\s*=.*/minclass = 3/' /etc/security/pwquality.conf
grep -q '^minclass' /etc/security/pwquality.conf || echo 'minclass = 3' >> /etc/security/pwquality.conf
